The test image shows a tomato leaf with multiple circular to oval lesions. Key features:
- Dark brown/black centers with lighter gray-tan surrounding tissue
- Concentric ring or zoning pattern in larger lesions
- Multiple lesions of varying sizes on the same leaf
- Small dark specks visible in lesion centers (possible pycnidia)
- No prominent yellow halos
- Lesion along the midrib follows vein shape

Top candidates: **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch** (circular gray lesions with dark pycnidia centers) or **Early_Blight** (larger dark brown lesions with concentric rings).

Using my 1 reference view on Septoria:

The Septoria reference shows very small, numerous tiny spots - much smaller than the lesions in the test image. The test image has:
- Larger lesions (clearly >1/8 inch)
- Prominent dark centers with surrounding lighter tissue showing concentric rings (target/bulls-eye pattern)
- Fewer but larger lesions

This rules out Septoria. The larger dark lesions with concentric rings match **Early_Blight** (Alternaria solani), which the knowledge base describes as "larger and darker brown than Septoria leaf spots and display concentric rings."

No fuzzy gray spore mass (Gray Mold), no yellow halos with tiny specks (Bacterial Speck), and no mosaic/bronzing patterns (viral diseases)."}
